title: Sifted homotopy colimits under the associative-algebra forgetful functor
statement:
Use the infinity-category, smallness and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and the model-category, biclosed monoidal product and nonsymmetric monoid-axiom definitions of [lem-coef-associative-algebra-model-transfer]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a combinatorial biclosed monoidal model category with cofibrant tensor unit and that monoid axiom, equipped with the transferred model structure on its strict associative unital algebras from that node. Suppose moreover that $\mathcal M$ is left proper (pushout of a weak equivalence along a cofibration is a weak equivalence) and tractable (there is a set of generating cofibrations between cofibrant objects). Write $W$ for its weak equivalences and $\widehat W$ for the algebra morphisms whose underlying maps lie in $W$. The forgetful functor induces
$$U_\infty:\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal M)[\widehat W^{-1}]_\infty\longrightarrow\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty.$$
For every small ordinary category $I$ whose ordinary nerve $N(I)$ is sifted, $U_\infty$ preserves $N(I)$-indexed colimits. Here sifted means that colimits in spaces indexed by $N(I)$ commute with finite products. In particular $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ is sifted and $U_\infty$ preserves geometric realizations, namely colimits of coherent simplicial diagrams, where $\Delta$ is the category of nonempty finite ordered sets and order-preserving maps.

source.place: Definition 3.18 and Lemma 3.19; Higher Topos Theory Lemma 5.5.8.4 for the geometric-realization indexing shape. The nonsymmetric monoid axiom is used with arbitrary auxiliary objects as in Muro Definition 9.1.
